prs.title: feat(tui): select text with the mouse and copy it on release
prs.body:
## What

Drag with the mouse in the TUI to highlight text, and it is copied to the clipboard on release, with a status bar confirmation. This supersedes #154, which left selection to the terminal: that selection ran across panes and borders, and copying was a manual step.

- **Selection** works on the rendered frame, so every tab gets it. A drag stays inside the bordered pane it started in, and what is highlighted is what gets copied.
- **Clipboard**: text goes out through OSC 52 and through `pbcopy`, `wl-copy`, `xclip` or `xsel`. Native tools are skipped over SSH, where they would fill the remote clipboard.
- **Status message**: says "Copied" only when a native tool confirmed it. OSC 52 gives no acknowledgement, so that case says the text was sent to the terminal.
- **Wheel**: mapped to Up/Down, because capturing the mouse stops the terminal from doing that translation.
- **Clearing**: a click or any key clears the selection. Esc clears it without quitting.
- **Native selection**: still available with the terminal's bypass modifier (usually Shift, or Option in iTerm2).

## Testing

- `cargo fmt --check`, CI's clippy, check and test commands, plus new unit tests in `crates/ui/src/selection.rs`.
- Drove the real binary under tmux with raw SGR mouse events, using a stub `pbcopy`:
  - Text arrived through the stub and through OSC 52 (tmux buffer).
  - Highlight during and after the drag, cleared by a click.
  - Esc didn't quit, wheel moved in both directions, mouse mode was off after quitting.
  - Selection tried on each tab.

Not tested: a real `pbcopy`, the Linux tools, or terminal emulators other than tmux.

## Known limits

- A drag doesn't auto-scroll at the pane edge, so a copy covers at most what is on screen.
- Double-click word and triple-click line selection aren't included.
- A drag that starts on a horizontal border or panel title isn't inside a pane, so it selects across the whole screen.

prs.title: fix(tui): stop capturing the mouse so text selection and copy work
prs.body:
Dragging the mouse over the TUI did nothing useful: the text could not be selected, so there was no way to copy a log line or a path out of it without quitting. This PR makes mouse selection and copy work the way they do in Claude Code and most other TUIs.

## Cause

`run_wrkflw_tui` enabled crossterm's `EnableMouseCapture` at startup, which asks the terminal to send every click and drag to the application instead of handling it itself. The event loop only ever matched `Event::Key`, so those mouse events were read and dropped. The only observable effect of the capture was that the terminal's native drag-to-select and copy stopped working.

## Fix

- Leave mouse capture off. The terminal keeps handling selection, so dragging highlights text and the usual copy shortcut (Cmd+C, Ctrl+Shift+C, …) copies it.
- Drop the matching `DisableMouseCapture` on teardown.
- README notes that the TUI does not capture the mouse.

No in-app selection or clipboard code is needed for this: the terminal does the work, which is also how Claude Code behaves.

## Testing

- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p wrkflw-ui --all-features -- -D warnings` and `cargo check -p wrkflw-ui --no-default-features` are clean.
- `cargo test -p wrkflw-ui --all-features`: 75 passed, 0 failed.
- Drove the old and new binaries in a pseudo-terminal and compared the bytes they write at startup. The old binary emits the mouse-tracking enables (`?1000h`, `?1002h`, `?1003h`, `?1006h`); the new one emits none of them and still enters the alternate screen.
- Launched the new TUI in tmux: the Workflows tab renders and `q` exits cleanly.

## Not covered

- Mouse-wheel scrolling never worked (wheel events were captured and dropped) and still doesn't. Terminals that translate wheel to arrow keys in the alternate screen (iTerm2, kitty, WezTerm) now get scrolling for free, since the keys reach the TUI; others don't. Adding real wheel support would mean re-enabling capture and implementing in-app selection with OSC 52 copy, which is a bigger change than this fix.

prs.title: fix: close the gaps found testing the agent features
prs.body:
Testing the agent features from #152 on a small Python repo with a matrix, secrets and path filters showed the failure digest working well, but four problems would mislead an agent or send it the wrong way.

## Fixed

- **False skip reasons.** A README-only PR reported `branch 'main' did not match ["main"]`. The reason now names only the filter that rejected.
- **Missing secrets failed the run.** `${{ secrets.X }}` failed a `run:` step here but is empty on GitHub, and was already empty in `env:`. It is now empty everywhere, the step output names the secret, and `plan` lists `missing_secrets`. Provider failures other than "not found" still fail the step.
- **`validate` missed real mistakes.** New rules: `unknown-trigger-filter`, `unterminated-expression`, `undefined-step-reference`, `undefined-need-reference`, `undefined-matrix-key`. Matrices only known at run time are not checked.
- **`--event` was too strict.** It now needs a change set only when that event has a `paths:` filter. MCP gains `no_strict_filter` and `variables`.

Smaller fixes:

- Matrix legs that failed the same way fold into `also_failed_in`, ignoring durations.
- Workspace paths in step output are relative.
- `error_lines` keeps likely causes from above the tail.
- `--from-step` failures carry a `note`.
- Unnamed `uses:` steps report the action.
- A missing workflow file is an error, not a recorded run.
- Usage errors are JSON in JSON mode.

## Behaviour changes

All are listed in `BREAKING_CHANGES.md`. The ones to look at: `validate` can now fail files that passed, a workflow relying on a missing secret failing no longer fails, and code counting `failures` per matrix leg should read `jobs` instead.

## Testing

- `cargo test --workspace`: 1262 passed, 0 failed. New regression tests cover each fix.
- `cargo fmt --check` is clean.
- `cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings` is clean with `clone_on_copy` allowed. That lint fails in `continue_on_error_test.rs`, which this PR doesn't touch.
- The new validate rules raised nothing across 32 workflow files in this repo.
- Replayed the original scenario end to end with emulation, real Docker and an MCP stdio client.

## Not covered

- Duration folding only blanks words like `0.01s` or `12ms`. Legs that differ by a timestamp still show separately.
- Workspace paths are only made relative in events and stored step logs. TUI and `job.log` output keep absolute paths.
- Missing-secret warnings don't cover composite action steps.

prs.title: feat(ui): drag over text to copy it
prs.body:
## What changed

Drag in the chat or the protocol log to highlight text. Letting go copies it, as in Claude Code.

- A selection stays inside the pane it started in, so the sidebar is never copied.
- The highlight clears on a click, a key, the wheel or a resize.
- Copied text drops trailing spaces, blank rows at the ends, shared indent and the `▎` bar beside messages.
- Picking a message now happens on mouse release, so a drag doesn't pick one. A plain click behaves as before.
- Local Mac sessions also use `pbcopy`, because Terminal.app ignores OSC 52. This fixes `y` and `/me` there too. Over SSH, only OSC 52 is used.

## Known limitations

- A message that wraps on screen copies with a line break at each wrap.
- Dragging to the edge doesn't scroll, so only what's on screen can be copied.
- A selection marks a screen position, so a new message arriving mid-drag can shift what gets copied.
- The composer, sidebar and pop-up panels have no drag selection. The help screen still explains the Shift or Option route.

## Testing

- `cargo test` passes and clippy reports no warnings.
- The real debug binary was run in a pseudo-terminal with raw mouse sequences, and all 31 checks passed.
- Those checks covered exact text, backward drags, pane limits, clearing, click to pick, wrapped messages, the log pane, the real macOS clipboard, SSH behaviour and clean exit.
- Not tried by hand in Terminal.app, iTerm or any other real terminal emulator, or in tmux.

prs.title: feat(ui): recall sent messages with up and down in the composer
prs.body:
## Summary
- Up and Down in the composer walk through what you sent in the open conversation, like a shell. Enter sends the recalled line again.
- Each conversation has its own list, so a line can't be resent to the wrong chat. Messages come from stored history; slash commands are kept for the session only.
- Files and automated `@home`/`@ai` replies are left out. Repeated lines collapse, and `/clear` wipes that conversation's list.
- An unsent draft comes back when you press Down past the newest line.

## Changed shortcut
Up on an empty line no longer selects a message unless nothing has been sent in that conversation. Selecting moves to Alt-Up; Ctrl-Up and clicking still work. The footer, help screen and README are updated.

## Testing
- `cargo test`: 200 passed, 6 ignored
- `cargo clippy --all-targets`: clean
- Not tried in a real terminal. Alt-Up on macOS may need Option set to send Meta/Esc+.

prs.title: feat(home): Tuya lights and Android TV / Google TV sets
prs.body:
Adds two device backends to `@home`, each in its own commit.

## Tuya lights (Wipro and most white-label Wi-Fi bulbs)

- Local control on TCP 6668, protocol 3.3, 3.4 and 3.5. Pairing tries each and keeps the one the bulb answers.
- `/home tuya IP DEVICE_ID LOCAL_KEY` adds a bulb. The key comes once from the Tuya cloud account (Tuya IoT platform or tinytuya's wizard). Nothing reaches the cloud at runtime.
- Found by sweeping for port 6668, because many bulbs never broadcast. Plugs and anything else that isn't a dimmable light are refused.
- On/off, brightness, white temperature, colour, status and blink.

## Android TV and Google TV sets

- Found over mDNS. Pairing shows a six-character code on the TV, typed with `/home code CODE`. A mistyped code is caught before anything is sent.
- hopchat makes a certificate per TV and pins the TV's own, as it does for LG.
- Power with Wake-on-LAN, volume level, steps and mute, apps, HDMI inputs and media keys.
- Home Assistant's `androidtv_remote` entities are left out, so a TV isn't listed twice.

## Testing

- **Tuya:** frames and session keys match vectors produced by tinytuya 1.20.0. A stand-in bulb covers every protocol version, a wrong key, a plug, and firmware that wants data points named.
- **Android TV:** messages match protoc's encoding of the androidtvremote2 0.3.2 schema, and the pairing hash matches the reference formula. A stand-in TV over real TLS covers pairing, certificate pinning, power, volume, apps and refused links.
- **On real hardware, with a Xiaomi Mi TV (MZTU0):** discovery worked, it paired, and it reported status. It changed volume, and opened YouTube and a video. This testing found two bugs the stand-in missed, both fixed here: the TV rejected a client certificate marked for certificate signing only, and it refused `market://launch` app links.
- **Not verified on hardware:** Tuya control. Two Tuya v3.5 bulbs were found and identified on the LAN, but their local keys weren't available. The live Android TV check is `cargo test scan_for_android_tvs -- --ignored --nocapture`, which shows a pairing code on the TV.
- `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` is clean, and `cargo test --locked` passes 185 tests with 6 ignored.

## New dependencies

- **Tuya:** `aes`, `aes-gcm`, `hmac` and `crc32fast`.
- **Android TV:** `rsa` and `x509-cert` (with the `builder` and `hazmat` features) and `rand_core`. `sha2` gains its `oid` feature.
- All are pure Rust and add no system libraries. `num-bigint-dig` is optimised in dev builds, because RSA key generation is otherwise slow there.

prs.title: feat: make wrkflw usable by coding agents
prs.body:
Agents can only scrape colored text from wrkflw today, and that text is gone when the process exits. This PR gives them structured output, a recorded history of runs, and an MCP server.

## What's new

- **`--format json`** is a global flag. stdout carries only JSON and logs move to stderr. `run`, `watch` and `runs replay` emit NDJSON events, and other commands emit one document.
- **Structured validation issues** have a rule id, YAML path, line and fix hint. Human messages are unchanged.
- **Run history** lives in the new `wrkflw-runs` crate. Each run stores its record, per-step logs, git state, agent and intent. Commands are `wrkflw runs list|show|logs|failure|replay`.
- **Failure digests** give the failed step, script, exit code, env exported by earlier steps and output tail. They appear in `run_finished`, in `runs failure`, and on stderr in text mode.
- **`wrkflw plan`** reports trigger decisions, job order, matrix legs and steps without executing anything.
- **`wrkflw mcp serve`** provides 8 tools over stdio. Tools run the wrkflw binary, so they return exactly what the JSON contract promises.
- **Attribution** comes from `--intent`, `--agent`, `WRKFLW_AGENT` and Claude Code detection. MCP uses the client's name. A new TUI Runs tab shows it.
- **`--from-step`** resumes a job at a step, and `watch --format json` streams cycles and run events.
- **Agent docs** are `AGENTS.md`, `skills/wrkflw` and a Claude Code plugin manifest.

## Security fix included

Step output was never masked. Resolved secrets were not registered with the masker, and `mask()` had no production caller, so secrets printed by a step reached the terminal. Persisting logs would have written them to disk, so this PR fixes it at the source. `--variable` values are never stored, and run directories are owner-only.

## Please review

- **Default-on recording.** Runs now write to the local data directory, capped at 500. `--no-record` and `WRKFLW_NO_HISTORY=1` opt out. Logs can still contain secrets wrkflw doesn't recognise.
- **`--from-step` semantics.** Each run has a fresh workspace, so earlier outputs and files are missing. Only `actions/checkout` still runs.
- **`output` is delivered per step.** Step output arrives in `step_finished`, not line by line, because the runtimes capture it. Live chunks would need runtime changes.
- **Line numbers are best effort.** `serde_yaml` drops positions, so a text walker finds them. Flow-style YAML reports the parent key's line.
- **Failure digest env is limited.** It lists variables earlier steps exported, with secrets masked, not a full env diff.
- **TUI runs are recorded from the job execution path only.** The `execute_workflow_cli` path in the UI crate is unchanged.

`BREAKING_CHANGES.md` covers the behaviour changes, including the `7`/`8` TUI key move.

## Testing

- `cargo test --workspace`: 1,220 passed, 0 failed.
- New end-to-end tests in `crates/wrkflw/tests/agent_cli_test.rs` drive the real binary. They parse stdout strictly and cover history, secret masking, replay, retention, plan, watch and a full MCP session.
- Ran a failing workflow through real Docker. Exit codes, digest and history were correct.
- The Kubernetes runtime was not exercised with these changes.
- `agent_cli_test.rs` is Unix-only because its fixtures use POSIX shell. Windows CI builds and runs the rest of the suite.
- On Windows, run files use the data directory's default permissions, and a crashed run stays `running` instead of becoming `interrupted`.
